historical_references.reference: Annalia of Aventicum was a Gallic bishop who wrote a history of the Gauls from 450 to 511 AD. She is considered the first known female historian in Europe.
historical_references.context: Annalia was born in the Gallic town of Aventicum (modern day Avenches, Switzerland) and was educated in the monastery of Saint Symmachus. She became a bishop and wrote a history of the Gauls, which is an important source of information about the Germanic tribes and the Roman Empire in the region during this time.

historical_references.reference: Anne of Kiev, also known as Anna of Constantinople, was a princess of the House of Olgovich who married King Henry I of France in the late 11th century. She is considered a saint in the Orthodox Church and is revered as a patron of women and mothers.
historical_references.context: Anne was born in Kiev, the capital city of the Kievan Rus', and was the daughter of Prince Sviatopolk II of Kiev. She was married to Henry I of France in 1051 or 1052, becoming the first known queen of France. She was known for her piety and was revered as a saint in the Orthodox Church. Her relics are currently enshrined in the church of Sainte-Croix de la Bretonnerie in Paris.
